Subject: Post-demo recap + next steps (model-fit, evals, quantization)

Hi Alex — great to meet you and the FinWave team today. Quick recap and proposed next steps after the demo: 

Summary from our side:
- Primary goal you shared: reduce latency for document summarization pipeline while keeping regression risk below 2% on your accuracy evals.
- Target throughput: ~250 requests/minute during peak; latency SLO: p95 < 750ms.
- Current constraints: on-prem inference for regulated data, and procurement prefers a phased rollout.

Next steps we recommend (short timeline):
1) Evaluation plan: run our model-fit evals against your prompt set (attached) to surface quality deltas across model sizes and quantization profiles.
2) Trade study: AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8 — we'll provide throughput numbers and expected accuracy deltas for 2-3 candidate models.
3) Canary configuration: start with a 10% traffic canary pinned to a robust variant (FP16 or conservative AWQ) while monitoring your eval set.

Attachments included:
- redwood_eval_plan.pdf (evaluation framework & metrics)
- finwave_prompt_set_v2.json (your prompt set export)
- awq_vs_gptq_trade_study.xlsx (initial trade study template)

Questions for you:
- Can you confirm the eval dataset we should prioritize (sensitivity: summaries vs extraction)?
- Who should we loop in from procurement for initial contract language?

I'll schedule a 30-minute follow-up next week to review the first-pass eval results. Thanks — Marissa

Best,

Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + next steps (model-fit, evals, quantization)

Alex — thanks, and good call on prioritizing longer-form summaries. Answering your questions and adding context from our ops/ML team: 

Quick model & quantization guidance (candidate shortlist):
- Mistral-7B-Instruct (FP16 / conservative AWQ): best cost/latency balance; AWQ tends to preserve instruction-following on our head-to-heads.
- Llama2-13B (FP16 / GPTQ-4bit): higher baseline quality on extraction tasks; GPTQ 4-bit implementations can be more brittle on long-context summarization and sometimes require calibration prompts.
- Falcon-40B (FP16 / FP8 experimental): highest raw quality but much higher cost — FP8 still experimental and we recommend only for a controlled pilot.

Tradeoffs we typically surface:
- AWQ (4-bit): often gives the best throughput with smaller quality delta vs FP16 on instruction tasks, but results vary by model architecture and prompt distribution.
- GPTQ (4-bit): can be performant but more sensitive to per-layer calibration and may introduce subtle tokenization/precision regressions on long summaries.
- FP8: promising throughput and accuracy for some families, but still experimental on many kernels and may have compatibility issues across hardware.

Benchmark/links attached: we've included an initial trade-study spreadsheet and a text file with public benchmark links for A10G/A100 runs and our internal p95 numbers. Dev — can you add the deeper latency microbenchmarks to the Drive link and call out warm vs cold start numbers?

Recommendation for the eval run:
- Run Mistral-7B-Instruct (FP16 baseline) vs Mistral-AWQ-4bit and Llama2-13B (FP16) vs Llama2-GPTQ-4bit on your labeled summary set.
- Measure accuracy deltas (ROUGE/EM/Custom scoring), hallucination rate, and the p95 latency on the target hardware (A10G preferred).
- If AWQ shows <=1.5% regression and p95 improves by >30% vs FP16, we propose a staged canary with AWQ at 10-20% traffic.

Attachments in this email: awq_vs_gptq_trade_study.xlsx, benchmark_results_links.txt

I'll get the SOW template and a pricing thumb for a small Dedicated pool to Procurement by Monday.

On canary config: we typically recommend:
- 10% traffic to AWQ variant for 72 hours
- Continuous eval against the labeled set and automated rollback if hallucination/regression spike >2%

Best,
Marissa
